explicit_validation.explanation: Both LLM and human evaluations are conducted but they serve different purposes - human annotations are used to verify perturbation impacts and provide ground truth for expected effects, not to directly validate LLM evaluation scores against human judgments. No correlation or agreement metrics are reported comparing LLM and human scores on the same instances.

prompts.notes: Prompts shown in tables throughout the paper, including GPT-4 construction prompts and evaluation prompts following Chiang and Lee (2023b) format. GPT-4 used for data construction in 10-shot settings.

inter_annotator_agreement.metric: annotation consistency (proportion of dominant option excluding uncertain)
inter_annotator_agreement.interpretation: 94.4% match rate with expectations for detailed definitions

guidelines.notes: Comparative evaluation with 'better than', 'worse than', 'as well as', or 'uncertain' options. Human annotations used to verify perturbation impacts beyond classification system guidance.

criteria_mapping.notes: Both LLM and human evaluations cover the same 11 common aspects, but they evaluate different aspects of the evaluation process - humans verify perturbation impacts while LLMs perform scoring evaluation. No direct comparison of scores on identical criteria instances.
